topics.topic: Operations subject to CLK-002, their boundary, and the wall-clock capture point
questions: Which requests or use-case paths count as operations that must take exactly one wall reading, which take none, and at what precise point—including on refusal paths—is that reading taken?
Must every portal operation take exactly one wall-clock reading, or only an operation that writes a portal-owned timestamp or makes a current-time comparison?
What exact boundary shares the single wall-clock instant when one request invokes authorization, a use case, cascaded mutations, and audit writing?
For each operation, at what ordered point is its sole wall-clock instant captured relative to request validation, authentication, Registry calls, persistence reads, and the final write?
Must every portal operation read the wall clock once, including pure reads and health checks, or only an operation that needs a fresh timestamp or current-time comparison?

quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.

authenticate_staff: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
judgement.why: P7 already judged the same clock-coverage and refusal-path timing question on these unchanged passages, with later operation notes defining the operation-level boundary.

authenticate_staff: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

topics.topic: Acceptance and interpretation of source-supplied offset-naive datetimes
questions: Must each source-supplied datetime contain an offset, or may an offset-naive datetime be accepted; if it is accepted, what instant does it denote?
Must a source-supplied datetime carry an offset, or may an offset-naive value be accepted and, if so, which timezone or instant does it denote?

quotes:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every
persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions). Calendar dates a source supplies — `document_date` of a
recognition, `payment_date` — are `date` values, kept as the supplied
calendar day: they carry no time or offset, are never converted to an
instant and never replaced by the clock's day; their accepted forms and checks, and where in an operation
its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7.
judgement.why: P4 already judged this same question: State 2 fixes instant preservation and UTC storage, while accepted input forms and validation belong to State 6.

topics.topic: Deployment outcome when installed-distribution metadata is unreadable or invalid
questions: What happens when the built image contains a discoverable Python distribution but the gate cannot obtain or parse that distribution's canonical name or installed version?
Does unreadable, missing, or invalid installed-distribution metadata make the check incomplete and block deployment even when no readable OSV entry can be matched to it?

quotes:
every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read once in
   that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data

A check that cannot
   complete does not pass: that deploy does not start the service, and a
   new deploy makes a new check.
judgement.why: An unreadable or unparsable installed identity prevents the required judgment of every installed distribution, so the check cannot complete and the deploy does not start.

topics.topic: OSV copy readability scope and handling of unreadable package identities
questions: What exactly must be read successfully before the OSV copy is usable: only the archive directory/index, every archive member, every OSV entry, or only entries determined to name installed distributions?
Does an OSV entry with an unreadable package identity block the deploy, invalidate the whole check, or get ignored as an entry not known to name an installed distribution?

quotes:
OSV's
   PyPI export archive, downloaded whole: the transfer completes without
   error, at the announced length when the server announces one, and the
   archive's index reads without error
   (a download that is not whole is a check that cannot complete; the gate
   has no other evidence of completeness and asks for none)

An entry naming
   an installed distribution that cannot be read this way blocks the deploy
   as if it listed that version; entries naming no installed distribution
   are not judged.
judgement.why: The text expressly limits archive-completeness evidence to transfer completion, announced length, and a readable index, then blocks unreadable entries only when they name an installed distribution and does not judge entries naming none.

topics.topic: Ownership, procedure, and binding verification for deployment-gate handoff
questions: Which receiving state owns the deployment-gate execution, what decided interface or procedure performs it, and which check confirms that the exact image digest, installed-distribution inventory, one fresh OSV copy, and verdict stay bound together?

Which receiving state owns the concrete release-gate execution, and which check confirms that the selected procedure inventories the bound image, reads one fresh whole OSV copy, applies the decided matching rules, and controls the start?

quotes:
The tool that runs the
   check is a deployment procedure, not a portal rule, carried to the
   deploy route.

- DEP-002: the deploy step judges every distribution installed in the
  built image, bound to the immutable digest of the
  platform image that starts (never a tag), against the one copy of OSV
  data read in the same deploy, and starts the service only on a passing verdict about
  that same image; a listed version, an advisory entry naming an installed
  distribution that cannot be read, an export that is not whole, a verdict from an earlier deploy, or a verdict about another image
  does not start it; its cases include a name that matches only after
  PEP 503 normalization, a version affected only through a range, and a
  withdrawn entry, which does not block
  [witness: verification:dependency_release_gate_client_portal].
judgement.why: State 2 fixes the release-gate behavior and its binding verification, while the concrete deployment procedure and tool are operational notes owned by State 7.

topics.topic: Authentication and transport-integrity requirements for the OSV copy
questions: What source-authentication and transport-integrity conditions must the OSV download satisfy, and which failures block the deploy?

quotes:
every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read once in
   that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data — OSV's
   PyPI export archive, downloaded whole: the transfer completes without
   error, at the announced length when the server announces one, and the
   archive's index reads without error
   (a download that is not whole is a check that cannot complete; the gate
   has no other evidence of completeness and asks for none) — against which every distribution is
   judged; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is
   reused.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts any complete, length-correct, readable archive even when its origin or authenticated transport cannot be established; another blocks unless the archive is authenticated as coming from OSV. The deploy operator and users awaiting the image observe whether the service starts.
judgement.why: The passage defines freshness and completeness evidence but leaves origin authentication, redirects, certificate failures, and substituted yet well-formed archives without a refusal rule.

topics.topic: Components covered by the sole-host-clock-reader invariant and its observable boundary
questions: Which executing components are forbidden to read a host clock directly, and what observable boundary must CLK-002 instrument?

quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.
judgement.why: The later module text defines the observable ownership boundary as portal modules: `system_clock` alone may read host clocks, while framework or dependency internals are not portal modules governed by this rule.

topics.topic: PEP 440 matching semantics for OSV affected-version membership
questions: Which PEP 440 matching relation decides exact affected-version membership and range membership, especially for local, pre-release, post-release, and epoch-bearing versions?

quotes:
A distribution has a known vulnerability when an OSV entry that is not
   withdrawn lists its installed version as affected: the entry's PyPI
   package name equals the distribution's name after PEP 503
   normalization, and its version, read by PEP 440, is one of the entry's
   affected versions or lies in one of its affected ranges.
judgement.divergence: One implementation compares parsed versions for exact PEP 440 equality and treats `1.0+vendor` as distinct from listed `1.0`; another applies PEP 440 specifier-style public-version matching and treats the local build as covered. The deploy operator observes whether the image starts.
judgement.why: PEP 440 supplies several comparison and specifier relations, but the rule does not select the relation used for exact-list or range membership involving local, pre-release, post-release, or epoch-bearing versions.

witness.initial: The built image contains distribution `example` version `1.0+vendor`, and a non-withdrawn OSV PyPI entry explicitly lists affected version `1.0`.
events: The deploy gate inventories the installed distribution.
The gate PEP 503-normalizes the package names and parses both versions under PEP 440.
The gate decides affected-version membership and whether to start the image.
outcomes: The image starts because parsed exact versions `1.0+vendor` and `1.0` are unequal.
The image does not start because matching affected public version `1.0` also covers local build `1.0+vendor`.
